2:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐν τῷ συνπληροῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς ἦσαν πάντες ὁμοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό·
2:1.targetText: And in the day of the Pentecost being fulfilled, they were all with one accord at the same place,

groups.note: Actual ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό supplies the same-place/together expression; place makes its local relation explicit without a separately written Greek place noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The temporal articular infinitive has no separate English article; the English day article corresponds to the actual day article.
N1904 prints ὁμοῦ, together. LSV with one accord follows the distinct TR ὁμοθυμαδόν adverb; their lexical identities are not exchanged.

unmappedTarget.reason: The TR prints ὁμοθυμαδόν, with one accord, while pinned N1904 has ὁμοῦ, together, at this position.

2:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἄφνω ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἦχος ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας καὶ ἐπλήρωσεν ὅλον τὸν οἶκον οὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι,
2:2.targetText: and there came suddenly out of the sky a sound as of a violent rushing wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting,

groups.note: The actual genitive wind noun in the comparison is rendered of a ... wind. The Greek case supplies of without a separate preposition.

2:3.sourceText: καὶ ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐφ’ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν,
2:3.targetText: and there appeared to them divided tongues, as it were of fire; it also sat on each one of them,

2:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες Πνεύματος Ἁγίου, καὶ ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις καθὼς τὸ Πνεῦμα ἐδίδου ἀποφθέγγεσθαι αὐτοῖς.
2:4.targetText: and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other tongues, according as the Spirit was giving them to declare.

groups.note: The actual genitive Spirit noun supplies the filling content, expressed with the Spirit; no separate Greek with preposition is printed.
The actual dative tongues gives the speaking medium, expressed with tongues; the English with belongs to that case-marked noun.

2:5.sourceText: Ἦσαν δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι, ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν·
2:5.targetText: And there were Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation of those under the heaven,

groups.note: Actual εἰς is used with the residence location, rendered in. Its source identity is retained rather than substituting ἐν.

2:6.sourceText: γενομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης συνῆλθεν τὸ πλῆθος καὶ συνεχύθη, ὅτι ἤκουον εἷς ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ λαλούντων αὐτῶν.
2:6.targetText: and the rumor of this having come, the multitude came together, and was confounded, because they were, each one, hearing them speaking in his proper dialect,

groups.note: LSV renders actual φωνή, sound/voice, as rumor in this sentence. This is the translation’s report wording for the printed sound noun, not a different φήμη source noun. Primary lexical senses: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/phone .
Actual ταύτης qualifies this sound in the genitive-absolute clause. English of this places the same demonstrative after its rumor rendering; no independent Greek of preposition is printed.
The actual dative article/dialect constituent gives the language relation in ... dialect. The adjective ἰδίᾳ supplies the distributive his proper wording without a separate Greek personal pronoun.

2:7.sourceText: ἐξίσταντο δὲ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον λέγοντες Οὐχὶ ἰδοὺ πάντες οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ λαλοῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι;
2:7.targetText: and they were all amazed, and wondered, saying to one another, “Behold, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?

unmappedTarget.reason: The first English all belongs to the opening amazed clause. Pinned N1904 lacks that extra πάντες there; its one actual πάντες qualifies these Galilean speakers later in the sentence.
LSV includes a reciprocal recipient phrase, corroborated by the TR πρὸς ἀλλήλους wording, absent from pinned N1904 here.

2:8.sourceText: καὶ πῶς ἡμεῖς ἀκούομεν ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ ἡμῶν ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθημεν,

groups.note: The actual dative article/dialect construction carries the first in ... dialect relation; the following printed ἐν supplies the separate in which clause.

2:9.sourceText: Πάρθοι καὶ Μῆδοι καὶ Ἐλαμεῖται, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν, Ἰουδαίαν τε καὶ Καππαδοκίαν, Πόντον καὶ τὴν Ἀσίαν,

2:10.sourceText: Φρυγίαν τε καὶ Παμφυλίαν, Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς Λιβύης τῆς κατὰ Κυρήνην, καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες Ῥωμαῖοι,

groups.note: Actual ἐπιδημοῦντες is the visiting/sojourning participle, rendered substantivally as strangers. The real participial head remains, not a substituted stranger noun.
Actual Ῥωμαῖοι is the Roman personal designation, rendered of Rome with strangers; no separate Greek Rome place noun or of preposition is written.

2:11.sourceText: Ἰουδαῖοί τε καὶ προσήλυτοι, Κρῆτες καὶ Ἄραβες, ἀκούομεν λαλούντων αὐτῶν ταῖς ἡμετέραις γλώσσαις τὰ μεγαλεῖα τοῦ Θεοῦ;

2:12.sourceText: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες καὶ διηποροῦντο, ἄλλος πρὸς ἄλλον λέγοντες Τί θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι;
2:12.targetText: And they were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying to one another, “What would this wish to be?”

groups.note: Actual θέλει is the present wishing/wanting verb. English would ... wish renders that predicate with a modal auxiliary; the source is not a Greek conditional or future form.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces the quoted statement. English uses direct quotation without a separate that word.

2:14.sourceText: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος σὺν τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐπῆρεν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπεφθέγξατο αὐτοῖς Ἄνδρες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Ἱερουσαλὴμ πάντες, τοῦτο ὑμῖν γνωστὸν ἔστω, καὶ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μου.
2:14.targetText: and Peter having stood up with the Eleven, lifted up his voice and declared to them: “Men—Jews, and all those dwelling in Jerusalem! Let this be known to you, and listen to my sayings,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Peter, his voice, and my sayings are not separately expressed in these English phrases.

2:15.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὑμεῖς ὑπολαμβάνετε οὗτοι μεθύουσιν, ἔστιν γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας,

2:16.targetText: But this is that which has been spoken through the prophet Joel:

And I will give wonders in the sky above,

2:23.sourceText: τοῦτον τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βουλῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔκδοτον διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμων προσπήξαντες ἀνείλατε,

2:25.sourceText: Δαυεὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς αὐτόν Προορώμην τὸν Κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός, ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν, ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ.

2:42.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ, τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς.
2:42.targetText: and they were continuing steadfastly in the teaching of the apostles, and the fellowship, and the breaking of the bread, and the prayers.

groups.note: The actual dative article/teaching constituent supplies in the teaching with continuing; no independent Greek in preposition is printed.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an additional and before the breaking, corroborated by the TR καί wording absent at that position in N1904.

2:43.sourceText: Ἐγίνετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος· πολλά δὲ τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο.
2:43.targetText: And fear came on every soul, also many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles,

groups.note: The actual dative every-soul constituent gives the affected recipients, rendered on every soul without a separately written Greek on preposition.

Actual ἐγίνετο is singular imperfect become/happen with the neuter-plural wonders/signs subject. English were being done uses a plural passive-style expression; no separate ποιέω doing verb is printed.

2:44.sourceText: πάντες δὲ οἱ πιστεύσαντες ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά,
2:44.targetText: and all those believing were at the same place, and had all things common,

groups.note: Actual πιστεύσαντες is the aorist believing participle, while LSV uses believing. The source is not relabeled as a present participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula with the same-place phrase; N1904 has no separately printed be verb here.
LSV has an extra conjunction before had, reflected in the longer TR copula/conjunction wording; N1904 directly connects the place phrase with had.

2:45.sourceText: καὶ τὰ κτήματα καὶ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον καὶ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσιν, καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν.
2:45.targetText: and they were selling the possessions and the goods, and were parting them to all, according as anyone had need.

2:46.sourceText: καθ’ ἡμέραν τε προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, κλῶντές τε κατ’ οἶκον ἄρτον, μετελάμβανον τροφῆς ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ ἀφελότητι καρδίας,
2:46.targetText: Also continuing daily with one accord in the temple, also breaking bread at every house, they were partaking of food in gladness and simplicity of heart,

groups.note: Actual κατ’ οἶκον is the distributive house-by-house expression, rendered at every house; every belongs to that construction rather than an independently written πᾶς adjective.

2:47.sourceText: αἰνοῦντες τὸν Θεὸν καὶ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαόν. ὁ δὲ Κύριος προσετίθει τοὺς σῳζομένους καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
2:47.targetText: praising God, and having favor with all the people, and the LORD was adding those being saved every day to the Assembly.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows the TR τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ church/Assembly phrase. Pinned N1904 has no church noun here; its ending ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό is accounted at the adjacent LSV 3:1, not used as a substitute Assembly head.

sourceMoved.reason: N1904 places ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό at the end of 2:47 with the adding/saved clause. TR places this same phrase at 3:1, matching the displayed LSV at the same time there. Both the changed clause attachment and the English temporal wording are explicit; N1904 2:47 is not thereby labeled inherently temporal.
